Name: Chandoviciti
Detail: Several works bear this name; the metadata does not say which.

Name: Dramatic Fragments (buddhist)
Detail: A collection of fragments, taken to be Lüders's; the Śāriputraprakaraṇa is added from what is known of that collection, not from the metadata.

Name: Śivastuti
Detail: Whether Laṅkeśvara is a poet's name or Rāvaṇa as legendary author is not clear from the metadata.

Name: Revākhāṇḍa of the Vāyupurāṇa (RKV)
Detail: Two different texts go by the name Revākhaṇḍa; this one (RKV) is split from the Skandapurāṇa's (RKS), as GRETIL's sigla do. Its place in a parent purāṇa is disputed, so it is mapped to no parent.

Name: Skandapurāṇa: Revākhaṇḍa (RKS)
Detail: Split from the Revākhaṇḍa 'of the Vāyupurāṇa' (RKV): same name, different text.

Name: 108 Buddhist stotras
Detail: An anthology of 108 hymns whose titles the metadata does not give; mapped to a collection title only.

Name: Ahoratravratakathā-prose
Detail: Prose version; grouped with the verse Kathā as one work in two versions, though they may be separate compositions.

Name: Ahorātravratacaityasevānuśaṃsāvadāna
Detail: Kept apart from the Ahorātravratakathā: a different name and a much longer text on the same vrata.

Name: Buddhist stotras
Detail: A small anthology whose hymns the metadata does not name; mapped to a collection title only, apart from the '108 Buddhist stotras'.

Name: Ekādaśamukha
Detail: Ekādaśamukha grouped with Ekādaśamukhahṛdaya as two files of one dhāraṇī text; the shorter name may be another text.

Name: Fragments of Prajñāpāramitā texts (from 16 sources)
Detail: Fragments of several Prajñāpāramitā texts, which the metadata does not name; mapped to a collection title only.

Name: Larger Prajñāpāramitā
Detail: File name points to Choong's edition of part of the Gilgit Larger Prajñāpāramitā; which named Prajñāpāramitā it belongs under is a judgement call.

Name: Larger Prajñāpāramitā
Detail: Kept apart from the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā; the Gilgit 'Larger Prajñāpāramitā' may be the Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā. At 102 KB a part only.

Name: Mahāpratisarāvidyādhāraṇī
Detail: Grouped with the Mahāpratisarā as a shorter version or fragment of it (14 KB); could be a separate dhāraṇī text.

Name: Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra
Detail: The title names only the kārikā text, but the file is the same size (380 KB) as the -comm file, so it very probably carries Vasubandhu's Bhāṣya too; mapped to both on that evidence.

Name: Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśatārāsādhana
Detail: A 2 KB sādhana, not Vāgīśvarakīrti's treatise; it may be an extract from it or the same as one of the other two Tārā sādhanas.

Name: Patna Dharmapada
Detail: Mapped to the Dharmapada as its Patna recension; it could as well be counted a work of its own beside the Pali Dhammapada and the Udānavarga.

Name: Pratisarākalpadhāraṇī
Detail: Kept apart from the Mahāpratisarā; it may be an extract from it.

Name: Pratītyasamutpādavibhaṅgasūtra
Detail: Grouped with the Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra as two forms of the same short sūtra; the titles differ and nothing confirms it.

Name: Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra
Detail: See the Pratītyasamutpādavibhaṅgasūtra item.

Name: Sabhikasaugataśāsanapravrajyāvratacaraṇaparivarta
Detail: The title is a chapter name (parivarta); the larger work is not named in the metadata, so it stands as a title of its own for now.

Name: Harināmacintāmaṇi
Detail: Bhaktivinoda's Harināmacintāmaṇi is a Bengali work; kept as a work since GRETIL files it among Sanskrit texts, but it may be ancillary (not Sanskrit) or a Sanskrit rendering.

Name: Śivasūtra with vārttika
Detail: The vārttika is not named; taken as Bhāskara's Śivasūtravārttika, though Varadarāja's is possible.

Name: Hetvābhāsadaśaka
Detail: The author field gives a description, not a name; kept as a person because it points to one man, but he is unidentified.

Name: Pradeśasaṃgraha
Detail: I do not know this work; Govind Kaul may be its author or its compiler.

Name: Abhisamayālaṃkāravivaraṇa
Detail: No author given. Taken as Haribhadra's shorter commentary (the Vivṛti, called Sphuṭārthā) in another edition, and so grouped with the 'vṛttiḥ sphuṭārthā' file; it could be a different commentary on the Abhisamayālaṃkāra.

Name: Bhavasaṃkrāntiṭīkā
Detail: This Maitreyanātha is kept apart from the Maitreya of the Abhisamayālaṃkāra and Madhyāntavibhāga, as Pandit does; the name alone would join them.

Name: Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi
Detail: No author and no qualifier. Taken as Ratnakīrti's Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi, presumably the anvayātmikā that pairs with the vyatirekātmikā files; Dharmottara's work of the same name does not survive in Sanskrit.

Name: Sekoddeśa
Detail: The Sekoddeśa is a Kālacakra scripture; Nāropa wrote its ṭīkā. The small file looks like the verses alone, so the item is mapped to the Sekoddeśa and the title is left authorless, though the metadata calls Nāropa the author. It may instead be (part of) the Sekoddeśaṭīkā.

Name: Viṃśikāvṛtti
Detail: 'Viṃśikāvṛtti' grouped with Vasubandhu's Viṃśatikāvṛtti; the file is very small (under 3 kB), so it can hold only a fragment of the vṛtti or the verses alone.

Name: Sāṃkhyakārikā with Śaṃkara's Jayamaṅgalā commentary
Detail: The 'Śaṃkara' of the Jayamaṅgalā is split from the Advaitin Śaṅkara of the Vedānta items: generally held a different author (Śaṅkarārya), and Pandit keeps a separate record.

Name: Aṣṭāṅganighaṇṭu
Detail: Vāhaṭa is a form of Vāgbhaṭa and is grouped with the author of the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya, as an ascription; the nighaṇṭu may be by a later Vāhaṭa.

Name: Bower Manuscript
Detail: A manuscript, not a work: it holds several texts (the Navanītaka and others) that the metadata does not list. Kept as one title under the manuscript's name.

Name: Rasādhyaya, 1-302+com with Ṭīkā
Detail: Verses with a ṭīkā; the metadata names neither author. Kaṅkālayogin for the verses and Merutuṅga for the ṭīkā are given from memory and need checking.

Name: Dharmapada
Detail: g:t0177: The Patna recension, kept under Dharmapada as its reader had it; it could be counted a work of its own beside the Pali Dhammapada and the Udānavarga.

Name: Fragments of Prajñāpāramitā texts
Detail: g:t0194: A GRETIL gathering of fragments of several unnamed Prajñāpāramitā texts, not a work; kept as an entity of its own.

Name: Larger Prajñāpāramitā
Detail: g:t0302: Left as an entity of its own: the Gilgit 'Larger Prajñāpāramitā' may belong with the Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā or the Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā, neither of which is in this window.

Name: Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśatārāsādhana
Detail: g:t0360: Kept apart from Vāgīśvarakīrti's Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśa (a 2 KB anonymous sādhana, not the treatise) and from the two other Mṛtyuvañcana Tārā sādhanas, whose names differ; it may be an extract or the same as one of them.

Name: Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra
Detail: g:t0449: One dossier, one reader's entry: its two items (…ādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra and …vibhaṅgasūtra) are taken as two forms of the same short sūtra on the twelve links; nothing independent confirms it.

Name: Revākhaṇḍa
Detail: g:t0491: Dossier split: GRETIL's sigla RKV and RKS mark two different texts called Revākhaṇḍa, with different parent-purāṇa claims. The reader's part_of Vāyupurāṇa is kept, though the claim is disputed; hence low. | Split d0482: GRETIL's sigla RKV and RKS mark two different texts of the same name, and the reader kept them apart. part_of left null because the reader's note says the parent is disputed (the member itself says Vāyupurāṇa).

Name: Revākhaṇḍa
Detail: g:t0492: Dossier split: GRETIL's sigla RKV and RKS mark two different texts called Revākhaṇḍa. Kept as a title of its own within the Skandapurāṇa, as a khaṇḍa known as a work in its own right; hence low. | Split d0482: RKS, a different text from RKV. Kept as a title of its own within the Skandapurāṇa, as the reader made it, since it circulates as a work; by the rule on divisions it could instead be folded into the Skandapurāṇa (d0570), whose member reads the same item as its part 'Revākhaṇḍa'.

Name: Sabhikasaugataśāsanapravrajyāvratacaraṇaparivarta
Detail: g:t0499: A parivarta (chapter) of an unnamed larger Buddhist narrative work; the parent is not in the window, so it stands alone.

Name: Bhartṛhari
Detail: g:p0039: The grammarian of the Vākyapadīya and the poet of the Śatakatraya are kept as one person: tradition identifies them, Pandit has a single record for both, and nothing in the metadata separates them. Modern scholarship often distinguishes the two; if they are to be split, the split is by member (p79 the poet, p_bhartrhari the grammarian).

Name: Maitreyanātha
Detail: g:p0157: Dossier d0151 split: the Bhavasaṃkrāntiṭīkā is a later commentary and not one of the five treatises, and Pandit keeps this Maitreyanātha as a record of his own; the name alone would join him to Maitreya.

Name: Prince of Koṭiliṅgapura
Detail: g:p0194: The author field is a description, not a name: an unidentified prince of the Kodungallur house.

Name: Śaṅkarārya
Detail: g:p0220: Kept apart from the Advaitin Śaṅkara (d0209): the Jayamaṅgalā on the Sāṃkhyakārikā is generally held to be by another Śaṅkara, and Pandit has a separate record, though the colophon calls him a pupil of Govinda.

Name: Sagarvihangam
Detail: Taken as a modern Sanskrit translation made from Meera Bhatt's Gujarati version of a foreign book; the roles of the four names are a guess.

Name: Granthtrai
Detail: A volume of three works that the metadata does not name; the collective title stands for them.

Name: Tithinirnay
Detail: The catalogue's author is taken as the modern editor; the Tithinirṇaya's own author is not given.

Name: Katharatnakar
Detail: The well-known Kathāratnākara is Hemavijaya Gaṇi's (1600 CE); the catalogue names Hemahaṃsa Gaṇi, perhaps by a slip. The title is given Hemavijaya, the name kept as written.

Name: Aatma ka Darshan
Detail: Hindi title from Jain Vishva Bharati; it may carry old texts with translation, but the metadata names none.

Name: Panch Stotrani
Detail: Five stotras that the metadata does not name; the catalogue's author is taken as the modern editor.

Name: Mohonmulanvadsthanakam
Detail: Both names are taken as modern editors of an older tract; one of them may be its author.

Name: Nayamrutam
Detail: Taken as a modern volume of older naya texts, with the catalogue's author as its editor.

Name: Pani Piyush Payasvini
Detail: The metadata does not show what kind of book this is.

Name: Adhyatmopnishat Prakaranam Savrutti
Detail: Which Adhyātmopaniṣad this is, and who wrote the vṛtti, are guesses: taken as Yaśovijaya's text with a modern vṛtti by Trailokyamaṇḍanavijaya.

Name: Siddhant Chandrika Purvarddham
Detail: The Siddhāntacandrikā is taken as Rāmāśrama's Sārasvata grammar; 'Ramsharma' may be its editor or a slip for the author. The year 1800 is doubtful.

Name: Kirtikala
Detail: Kīrtikalā is taken as a modern commentary on a work of Hemacandra, who is author of the base text only; which base text is not said.

Name: Agam 44 Chulika 01 Nandi Sutra
Detail: 'Chandrasuri' on a Nandīsūtra is taken as Śrīcandrasūri, author of a gloss on Haribhadra's Nandīvṛtti, and as a different man from the 'Chandrasuri' of j:001564; both points are uncertain.

Name: Samaysara
Detail: Titled Samayasāra, but with Mahāprajña as author in 1991 this is taken to be his Hindi discourses on Kundakunda's Samayasāra, not an edition of it.

Name: Jain Yoga ke Sat Granth
Detail: An anthology of seven older Jain yoga texts with Hindi translation; the metadata names none, so the collection stands as the title. Dulaharāja is its editor and translator.

Name: Yogakshema Sutra
Detail: Taken as a modern Hindi book despite 'Sutra' in the title.

Name: Devdravyadisiddhi Aparnam Bechar Hitshiksha
Detail: An early 20th-century polemical tract; its language and whether the two laymen are authors or publishers cannot be told from the metadata.

Name: Stavanavali
Detail: A hymn collection whose contents and language the metadata does not give.

Name: Swarup Deshna Vimarsh
Detail: Taken as a modern Hindi volume of discussion on Viśuddhasāgara's discourses on the Svarūpasambodhana; it may carry that text.

Name: Shantinath Charitram
Detail: Which Śāntināthacaritra this is cannot be told; the catalogue's author is taken as a 20th-century editor.

Name: Jin Darshan Chovisi
Detail: A caubīsī is a set of twenty-four hymns to the Jinas, but the metadata does not say whose or in what language; it may be a picture book.

Name: Agam Sudha Sindhu Part 11
Detail: Filed under 'Chedasūtra > Kalpasūtra'. Taken as the Paryuṣaṇākalpa and so split from the Bṛhatkalpa of j:004353, since the series' other Chedasūtras fall in Part 09; it could be the Bṛhatkalpa.

Name: Jain Gyan Gun Sangraha
Detail: Taken as a 1936 vernacular compendium of Jain lore, not a Sanskrit work; the metadata does not settle it.

Name: Narbhavdrushtantopnaymala
Detail: Jinendrasūri is taken as the later name of Jinendravijaya Gaṇi and as editor; he could be the author, and the two could be different persons.

Name: Karmgranth tatha Sukshmarth Vicharsar Prakaran
Detail: 'Karmagrantha' grouped with Devendrasūri's, though the volume may hold one of the older Karmagranthas; the catalogue's author is the 1974 editor.

Name: Sthaviravali
Detail: 'Hivadacharya' read as Himavadācārya and the item as the Sthavirāvalī ascribed to him; 12 pages with three modern names may instead be a discussion of that text.

Name: Prakaran Pushpmala
Detail: Collection of prakaraṇas whose contents are not named; Ratnasiṃhasūri taken as author and Devavijaya as editor.

Name: Parshwanath Paramparaya Itihas
Detail: Taken as a modern Sanskrit history from the Sanskrit form of the title; could be ancillary. Śukla's role is a guess.

Name: Chakshurprapyakaritawad
Detail: Punyapālasūri taken as modern editor; he may instead be the author or commentator.

Name: Prakrit Shabda Rupavali
Detail: Prākṛtaśabdarūpāvalī: taken as modern learning material (Prakrit paradigms after Hemacandra), so ancillary and Hemacandra left unplaced.

Name: Madhyam Siddh Prabha Vyakaranam
Detail: Jinendrasūri taken as editor, as on the Kāvyaṣaṭka; the grammar's author is not given.

Name: Arshbhiyacharit Vijayollas tatha Siddhasahasra Namkosh
Detail: Three works of Yaśovijaya Upādhyāya in one volume (1976). The catalogue's 'Yashovijay-2' is read as the modern editor Yaśovijaya, set apart by the homonym mark from 'Yashovijay Upadhyay'; if the mark means the Upādhyāya himself, he is the author.

Name: Prakrit Vyakaranam
Detail: Which Prakrit grammar this is, and whether Saṃyamasāgara is editor or author, the metadata does not say.

Name: Kalplatavatarika
Detail: Kalpalatāvatārikā read as Vijayāmṛtasūri's commentary on Yaśovijaya's Syādvādakalpalatā, which the edition would carry; from memory, not from the metadata.

Name: Bramhopnishad
Detail: Not grouped with the Atharvavedic Brahmopaniṣad: a Jain monk's 2012 publication, probably his own commentary on an unnamed older text.

Name: Mantungashastram
Detail: The work and which Mānatuṅga is meant are not identified.

Name: Nyayasamucchaya
Detail: Nyāyasamuccaya read as Hemahaṃsa Gaṇi's collection of the Siddhahema paribhāṣās (Nyāyasaṅgraha) in Vijayalāvaṇyasūri's edition with his own commentaries; Lāvaṇyasūri is editor and commentator, not the compiler. From memory, not from the metadata.

Name: Saptabhangimimansa
Detail: Taken as a modern Sanskrit composition by the monk named; he could be an editor.

Name: Bruhad Dharana Yantra
Detail: Astrological tables; whether an old text or a modern compilation is not clear.

Name: Atmashuddhipayog
Detail: Kept apart from Śuddhopayoga (j:008664) on the different title and page count; they may be one work.

Name: Jain Syadvadamuktawali
Detail: Buddhisāgara kept as author as the catalogue has it; he may only have edited an older Syādvādamuktāvalī.

Name: Nitya Mangal aur Gautamswami Ka Ras
Detail: Devotional booklet with a Hindi title: daily auspicious recitations and the vernacular Gautamasvāmī Rāsa; taken as ancillary, though it may hold Sanskrit or Prakrit recitations.

Name: Parmatma Darshan
Detail: Probably largely Gujarati; kept as a work because the catalogue files it as Sanskrit.

Name: Snatrapooja
Detail: Probably a vernacular pūjā; kept as a work because the catalogue files it as Sanskrit.

Name: Tattva Bindu
Detail: Possibly Gujarati; kept as a work because the catalogue files it as Sanskrit.

Name: Yugadi Vandana
Detail: Contents not identified; taken as a devotional collection compiled by the monk named.

Name: Kavyanushasanam
Detail: Taken as Hemacandra's Kāvyānuśāsana (sūtra text, 92 pages) in a modern Jain edition; Vāgbhaṭa's work of the same name is possible.

Name: Kriya kosha
Detail: Modern topical cyclopaedia of canonical passages on kriyā with Hindi (1969); taken as a reference compilation, not a Sanskrit work.

Name: Samanyanirukti Chandrakala kalavilas Tika
Detail: Sāmānyanirukti with the two commentaries Candrakalā and Kalāvilāsa; both are put under Vāmācaraṇa, though one may be by another hand.

Name: Samta Sagar Charitam
Detail: A 2004 work on a modern monk, so the name is a modern Hemacandrasūri, kept apart from the 12th-c. Hemacandra ('Hemchandracharya').

Name: Vaddhamana Deshna
Detail: The Prakrit title points to Śubhavardhana's Vaddhamāṇadesaṇā, the named Rājakīrti to the Sanskrit prose version; taken as one work. Sūracandra's part is unknown.

Name: Kshetra Sparshana Prakaranam
Detail: The contemporary monk is taken as editor of an older prakaraṇa, but he may be its author.

Name: Jambuswami Charitra
Detail: Which Jambūsvāmicarita this is, and whether Vimla Jain edits, translates or retells it, the metadata does not say.

Name: Jain Siddhanta
Detail: Taken as a Hindi exposition of Jain doctrine by the Sthānakavāsī Upādhyāya Ātmārāma (1915), not a Sanskrit work.

Name: Jain Ratnasara
Detail: Taken as a compendium of rites and hymns compiled by the yati; how much of it is Sanskrit is not known.

Name: Jain Vrat Katha Sangraha
Detail: A 39-page collection of vrata stories; the catalogue's author is taken as compiler but may be only the publisher, and the language may be Hindi.

Name: Chattrish Bol Sangraha
Detail: A Sthānakavāsī collection of thirty-six doctrinal 'bol' (topic lists) in Hindi, taken as learning material rather than a Sanskrit work.

Name: Abhidhan Chintamani Nammala Tika
Detail: The ṭīkā is not named; it is taken as Hemacandra's own, since no other author is given.

Name: Hemchandra Kosh
Detail: 'Hemacandrakośa' is taken as the Abhidhānacintāmaṇi, the usual sense of that name in early prints; it could be another of Hemacandra's lexica (Anekārthasaṃgraha).

Name: Atha Vedanga Prakash
Detail: Taken as one part (69 pp.) of Dayānanda Sarasvatī's Vedāṅgaprakāśa, a grammar primer in Sanskrit and Hindi; it could as well be counted as learning material.

Name: Anyokti Shatakam
Detail: Darśanavijaya is taken as the author, but in a 1937 print the name may be that of a modern editor.

Name: Aradhana Swarup
Detail: Neither the nature of the text nor the role of the name is clear from the metadata.

Name: Arthsangraha
Detail: Taken as Laugākṣi Bhāskara's Arthasaṃgraha in a Bengal edition (1821 Śaka = 1899/1900), whose 474 pages point to a commentary; the catalogue's author would then be its editor or commentator, not the author of the Arthasaṃgraha.

Name: Ashtaprakari Pooja Kathanak
Detail: 'Aṣṭaprakārī-pūjā-kathānaka' is taken as the Vijayacandrakevalicaritra of Candraprabha Mahattara, whose hero the catalogue gives as author.

Name: Atharvaved Samhitaya
Detail: The genitive title ('Atharvavedasaṃhitāyāḥ …') and 116 pages suggest an index or a portion of the Saṃhitā rather than the whole text.

Name: Bruhat Paryushananirnay
Detail: Taken as a modern Hindi polemic on the date of Paryuṣaṇa (1922), not a Sanskrit work.

Name: Chandrayash Charitram
Detail: Which Vardhamānasūri is meant is not clear; grouped with the one on j:020345 for want of evidence to split.

Name: Dangvopakhyanam
Detail: Identified from the title alone; language and source are not stated.

Name: Drushtant Shatakam
Detail: Bhūpendrasūri is taken as editor or expositor of an older Dṛṣṭāntaśataka; he may instead be its author.

Name: Dwadash Parv Vyakhtyana Bhashantaram
Detail: A vernacular translation (bhāṣāntara) of a Dvādaśaparvavyākhyāna, taken as Kṣamākalyāṇa's because the publisher is Kharataragaccha.

Name: Dwadashanupreksha Bhasha Tika Sahit
Detail: Taken as the twelve-anuprekṣā section of Śubhacandra's Jñānārṇava with a Hindi commentary; the metadata does not say which Śubhacandra or which text.

Name: Dwait Samrajya
Detail: Known only by its title.

Name: Gautamswamyashtakam
Detail: The aṣṭaka is taken as the traditional hymn and the modern monk as its editor and expositor (58 pp. for eight verses); he may instead have composed it.

Name: Geetashastrasya Pratikandam
Detail: 'Gītāśāstrasya pratikāṇḍam' with no author: perhaps a work on the Bhagavadgītā, but the metadata does not say what this 410-page book is.

Name: Ghantakarna Pratishtha Vidhi_
Detail: Which Vardhamānasūri is meant is not clear; grouped with the one on j:020143 for want of evidence to split.

Name: Gurugun Shattrinshat Shattrinshika
Detail: The catalogue's author is taken as the modern editor; the work is put under Ratnaśekharasūri from knowledge. Which Buddhisāgara is meant is uncertain (grouped with the Kharatara Buddhisāgara Gaṇi; the Tapāgaccha Buddhisāgarasūri is possible).

Name: Hetvabhas Savyabhichar
Detail: A Navyanyāya section on the savyabhicāra fallacy; 'Gangadhar' may be a slip for Gadādhara, in which case this is part of the Gādādharī.

Name: Hirvijaysuri Jivan Charitra
Detail: A 28-page modern life of Hīravijayasūri (1961), taken as a vernacular booklet rather than a Sanskrit work.

Name: Hitopdesh
Detail: Grouped with Nārāyaṇa's Hitopadeśa on the title alone. 'Kanthsuri' is unexplained: if it names an author, this is a different, Jain Hitopadeśa. Both roles are guesses.

Name: Jain Ling Nirnay
Detail: No author and no sign of the language; may be a modern vernacular tract.

Name: Jambuswami Charitam
Detail: Grouped with j:020401 on title and near-equal size; the metadata names only a modern monk, who may be editor or the author of a new Sanskrit rendering, in which case this is a different composition.

Name: Jinduttasuri Charitram Purvarddha
Detail: The layman named is probably the publisher or patron, not the author; 'editor' is the nearest role. The author is not given.

Name: Kusumavali
Detail: What this 1943 'Kusumāvali' holds is not clear from the metadata; Hemacandra is taken as the 12th c. polymath.

Name: Kamghat Kathanakam
Detail: The Kāmaghaṭakathānaka is an anonymous Jain tale; the name is taken as a modern editor or translator.

Name: Kshama Rushi
Detail: A 48-page booklet of 1921; it may be a vernacular retelling and so ancillary.

Name: Kulingivadanodgar Mimansa Part 01
Detail: A 1926 sectarian polemic; its language is not known, and it may be vernacular.

Name: Kushalchandrasuripatta Prashasti
Detail: Three names with nothing to tell their roles apart; the sūri is taken as author and the other two as those who brought the book out.

Name: Mahimna Stotra Tika
Detail: Taken as the Śivamahimnaḥstotra with an unnamed commentary; a Jain Mahimnaḥstotra is not ruled out.

Name: Mohan Sanjivani
Detail: Language and contents are not known; if it is a vernacular biography it is ancillary. Roles are a guess.

Name: Murtimandan
Detail: A modern polemic; its language is not known, and it may be Hindi and so ancillary.

Name: Nadigyan Tarangini
Detail: The name is taken as the Gujarati translator or publisher of an older treatise, not its author.

Name: Nandi Sutra Tika
Detail: The commentator is not named; probably Malayagiri's vṛtti.

Name: Niti Sangraha

Name: Rajvidya

Name: Rampanchdashi Satik

Name: Ransinh Charitram
Detail: The author's name is garbled or abbreviated and cannot be identified.

Name: Rekhaganit
Detail: Either a geometry schoolbook by this author (then ancillary) or an edition of the Sanskrit Rekhāgaṇita; the metadata does not settle it.

Name: Sadharmik Vatsalya Prakash

Name: Sagarotpatti

Name: Sanshay Timir Pradip
Detail: Taken as a modern Hindi doctrinal tract (1909).

Name: Saptapadi Shastra
Detail: The catalogue's author is taken as the modern editor of a Pārśvacandragaccha text; he may instead be its author.

Name: Sarva Dev Samanyo Dev Pujan Prayog
Detail: A modern ritual manual; whether the name is its author or compiler is a guess.

Name: Nar Vikram Charitram
Detail: An episode of Guṇacandra's Mahāvīracariya issued separately in Sanskrit; Śubhaṅkaravijaya is its redactor, entered as editor, though he could be counted as author of the rendering.

Name: Shanti Shloak Tika Tatha Anyamat Dushanam
Detail: Two short pieces in one booklet; Vikramavijaya is taken as their author, though he may be only the editor.

Name: Sharirik Mimansa Bhashye Part 01
Detail: The catalogue's author is the editor. 'Śārīrakamīmāṃsābhāṣya' is the formal title of both Rāmānuja's and Śaṅkara's bhāṣyas; read as Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya from the editor's name, and probably printed with a sub-commentary.

Name: Shauchnirnay Trayambakiya
Detail: 'Tryambakīya' in the title points to an author Tryambaka, who is not otherwise identified.

Name: Shripal Charitram
Detail: The catalogue's author is a contemporary editor; which Sanskrit Śrīpālacaritra this is the metadata does not say. Kept apart from the Prakrit Sirivālakahā of j:020748.

Name: Shvetambar Digamber Part 01 02
Detail: Taken as a modern Hindi book on the Śvetāmbara–Digambara division, parts 1–2.

Name: Sudha Sanchit
Detail: Work not recognised; the name may be its author or its compiler/editor.

Name: Tattva Nirnayprasad
Detail: Tattvanirṇayaprāsāda: a Hindi doctrinal and polemical treatise by Ātmārāma (Vijayānandasūri, d. 1896), edited by his disciple Vallabhavijaya. Not a Sanskrit work, though filed as Sanskrit; could instead be counted as a work.

Name: Tattvartha Sutram Part 01
Detail: Ghāsīlāla's Tattvārthasūtra with his Dīpikā and Niryukti (1973). His sūtra text is a Sthānakavāsī redaction of his own, grouped here with Umāsvāti's Tattvārthasūtra for want of evidence to split. The catalogue's author is the editor.

Name: Tattvavatar
Detail: Work not recognised; the first name is taken as author and Becaradāsa as editor.

Name: Tibba Ratnakar

Name: Tilak Manjri
Detail: Only 84 pages, so a fragment or first fascicle. Padmasāgara is taken as commentator; Lāvaṇyasūri is known for his Parāga commentary but may be only the editor here.

Name: Trinshshloki
Detail: No author; which Triṃśacchlokī this is cannot be told from the metadata.

Name: Uvvatbhashya

Name: Vedang Prakash
Detail: One part (77 pp.) of Dayānanda's Vedāṅgaprakāśa, which part is not stated. Grammar manuals in Sanskrit with Hindi exposition: counted as a work, but could be ancillary learning material.

Name: Vedang Prakash
Detail: Another part or parts (326 pp.) of the Vedāṅgaprakāśa; see j:020881.

Name: Vedant Chintamani
Detail: No author; which Vedāntacintāmaṇi this is cannot be told.

Name: Vedant Prakaranam
Detail: Work not recognised; the name may be author rather than editor.

Name: Vipak Sutra
Detail: The name is not recognised and is taken as the editor of the 1877 edition.

Name: Vishva Gunadarsh Champu
Detail: Neither name is the author, Veṅkaṭādhvarin. Both are taken as hands of the 1910 edition; 'Gangadev Bhatt' may be a commentator or a garbled name.

Name: Vividh Payannav Churi Tika
Detail: 'Various Prakīrṇakas with avacūri': a collection of several Prakīrṇakas, of which only the Catuḥśaraṇa is identified, by the catalogue's category. The others and the avacūri are not named.

Name: Vruddhi Ratnamala
Detail: Title and name coincide; he may be the compiler or the person honoured.

Name: Vruttabodh
Detail: Possibly a school primer rather than an old work.

Name: Yajurved Samhitaya

Name: Yamdand
Detail: Yamadaṇḍa: a Gujarati devotional poem of the Svāminārāyaṇa tradition, not a Sanskrit work though filed as Sanskrit; could instead be counted as a work.

Name: Yavanraj Vanshavali

Name: Kaysthiti Prakaranam

Name: Padarth Pradip
Detail: Work not recognised; probably a modern compilation, and he may be compiler rather than author. The catalogue's year '132' is the page count.

Name: Prakaran Ratna
Detail: A collection of prakaraṇas; kept apart from the Prakaraṇaratnākara (j:022320) of the same publisher, though they may be one series.

Name: Praman Paribhasha

Name: Jagat Kartutva Mimansa Prakaranam

Name: Vishva Kartutva Mimansa Evam Jagat Kartutva Mimansa
Detail: Two tracts in one book; which of them Suśīlasūri wrote is not clear from the metadata.

Name: Gacchayar Ppayanna
Detail: Roles guessed: Rājendrasūri as vernacular translator, Gulābavijaya as editor. Any Sanskrit ṭīkā printed with the text is not named.

Name: Jivan Shreyaskar Pathmala
Detail: A compilation whose contents the metadata does not name.

Name: Nandisutra Mahatmya
Detail: Not grouped with the Nandīsūtra: the title says Māhātmya, and whether the book is the sūtra or a tract on it cannot be told.

Name: Chandraprabh Charitram Part 01
Detail: Grouped by title with Vīranandin's Candraprabhacarita, but a Śvetāmbara editor and three times the length suggest Devendrasūri's Candraprabhacaritra instead.

Name: Chandraprabh Charitram Part 02
Detail: As Part 01: possibly Devendrasūri's Candraprabhacaritra, not Vīranandin's.

Name: Vijay Prashasti Sar
Detail: Taken as Vidyāvijaya's vernacular summary (sāra) of Hemavijaya's Vijayapraśasti, not the kāvya itself; Harshchandra Bhurabhai is the publisher.

Name: Vastusar Ratnapal Charitre

Name: Muldev Nrup Charitram
Detail: Whether Harṣavijaya is author or editor is not clear; taken as editor.

Name: Dharm Parikshano Ras

Name: Haimnutan Laghu Prakriya
Detail: Roles guessed: the ācārya as author, the paṇḍit as editor.

Name: Tattvabindu

Name: Karakmala
Detail: Roles guessed; the metadata does not say who wrote and who edited.

Name: Indriya Parajay Digdarshan
Detail: Taken as one of Vijayadharmasūri's vernacular -digdarśana tracts, not an old Sanskrit work.

Name: Bhram Vidhvansanam
Detail: A 19th-c. Rajasthani work, not Sanskrit; kept as a work.

Name: Bhota Prakasa

Name: Sutra Rahasyam

Detail: Title read as Sujāta-Vārtaka-ṛṣi-caritra.

Detail: An unidentified exposition of the Siddhāntakaumudī.

Detail: Ṣaṭkalyāṇakanirṇaya: taken as a modern Hindi gaccha polemic (part of Maṇisāgara's Bṛhatparyuṣaṇānirṇaya).

Name: Bruhat Paryushana Nirnay
Detail: Bṛhatparyuṣaṇānirṇaya: taken as a modern Hindi gaccha polemic.

Name: Harsh Hriday Darpanasya Dwitiya Bhag
Detail: Harṣahṛdayadarpaṇa, part 2: taken as a modern Hindi gaccha polemic.

Name: Lalita Dukhdarshak
Detail: A Gujarati play; catalogued as Sanskrit, perhaps a Sanskrit rendering.

Name: Saddharm Mandanam
Detail: Saddharmamaṇḍana: taken as a modern Hindi Sthānakavāsī polemic.

Detail: Roles of the two Śāstrīs are a guess.

Name: Tattvavetta
Detail: Tattvavettā (1954): taken as a modern Hindi book.

Name: Vastravarnasiddhi
Detail: Vastravarṇasiddhi: taken as a modern Hindi tract on the colour of monks' robes.

Name: Tattvarthadhigam Parishishtam
Detail: An appendix volume to an edition of the Tattvārthādhigamasūtra; it may be indexes only.

Name: Updeshsaptatika
Detail: No author given; grouped with Kṣemarāja's "navyā" Upadeśasaptatikā, but it may be Somadharmagaṇi's older work.

Name: Dhanya Charitam Padyam
Detail: Vijayānandasūri taken as editor, not author; a guess.

Detail: Kumudvijay is taken as the modern editor, which the metadata does not settle.

Detail: Lalitavijaya is taken as the editor of the 1915 edition. Which Saṅgrahaṇī this is, and so its author, is not said.

Name: Subodh Samachari
Detail: Macchindracharya is read as a garbled Śrīcandrācārya: the Subodhā Sāmācārī is Śrīcandrasūri's.

Name: Dhanna Shalibhadrano Ras
Detail: An Old Gujarati rāsa filed as Sanskrit; kept as a work, not ancillary. The catalogue's author is the publisher.

Name: Meghmala Vichar
Detail: The catalogue's author is the publisher. The language and author of this weather-lore text are not said.

Name: Vissthanakno Ras
Detail: An Old Gujarati rāsa filed as Sanskrit; kept as a work, not ancillary, and not grouped with Jinaharṣa's Sanskrit Viṃśatisthānakacarita. The catalogue's author is the publisher.

Name: Hingul Prakaran
Detail: The catalogue's author is the publisher. The ascription of the Hiṅgulaprakaraṇa to Vinayasāgara is from memory.

Name: Kumarpal Pratibodh Prabandh
Detail: The catalogue's author is a modern editor. The prabandha's author is not said, and it is kept apart from Jinamaṇḍana's Kumārapālaprabandha (j:600161).

Name: Arhan Mahapujan tatha Poshtik Mahapujan
Detail: The two rites are taken as extracts from Vardhamānasūri's Ācāradinakara, a title the metadata does not give; Anantacandra is taken as editor.

Name: Syadwad bhasha Devdharmpariksha Adhyatmopnishad Adhyatmikmatpariksha Yatilakshansamucchay
Detail: Five short works. The Syādvādabhāṣā is Śubhavijaya's and the other four Yaśovijaya's. The Ādhyātmikamataparīkṣā of this 138-page book is taken as his short Ādhyātmikamatakhaṇḍana, split from the Adhyātmamataparīkṣā of j:600058.

Name: Shripal Rajano Ras
Detail: An Old Gujarati rāsa filed as Sanskrit; kept as a work, not ancillary, and apart from the Sanskrit and Prakrit Śrīpāla works. The catalogue's author is the publisher.

Name: Chakkavattisa Kaha
Detail: Jayānandavijaya is taken as a modern editor; he could be the author of a modern Prakrit story.

Name: Paryushan Satparvashtanhika Vyakhyan
Detail: A translation (bhāṣāntara) of an Aṣṭāhnikavyākhyāna, grouped with Kṣamākalyāṇa's (j:600210) on the title alone; other works of this name exist.

Name: Adhyatmavichar Jeet Sangraha
Detail: A modern collection whose language and contents the metadata does not say; it may be ancillary.

Name: Sadhu Sadhvi Aradhana tatha Antkriya Vidhi
Detail: An 18-page ritual manual; Buddhimuni is taken as its compiler and kept apart from Buddhisāgara Gaṇi.

Detail: Neither the work nor this Bhadragupta is known to me; he may be a traditional ascription or a modern compiler.

Detail: Five pages only; Kalyāṇabodhisūri may be the author of a short modern work or the editor or commentator of an older Yogopaniṣad.

Detail: The author is left unplaced. The commentary printed is probably Abhayadeva's, but as the metadata does not name him it is not mapped.

Name: Pind Niryukti
Detail: The author is left unplaced. The commentary printed is probably Malayagiri's, but as the metadata does not name him it is not mapped.

Detail: The catalogue's author is the modern editor; which Candraprabhacarita this is the metadata does not say.

Name: Surdipikadi Prakaran Sangraha
Detail: A collection whose works are not identified; the collection itself is the title.

Name: Kalpsutram
Detail: The name is taken as the author of the Dānadīpikā commentary; it could instead be a modern editor (Dānavijaya, later Vijayadānasūri).

Name: Paryushanasthahnika Vyakhyan
Detail: Maṇivijaya is taken as the editor of an older Sanskrit sermon; he could be its author.

Name: Jiv Samas Arth Sahit
Detail: The Jīvasamāsa 'with meaning'; Rasika Muni is taken as the modern translator.

Name: Satik Gacchachar Prakirnak Sutram
Detail: The unnamed ṭīkā is grouped with Vānararṣi's (Vijayavimala's) commentary; Dānavijaya is taken as the modern editor, later Vijayadānasūri.

Name: Prakaran Sangraha
Detail: A collection naming no work; the collection itself is the title.

Name: Sukta Muktavali
Detail: Which Sūktamuktāvalī this is the metadata does not say; Bhūpendrasūri is taken as compiler and Gulābavijaya as editor.

Name: Surchandra Charitram
Detail: A single tale printed as a pamphlet; which Vardhamānasūri and which source work is not established.

Name: Sadaivvatsakumar Charitram
Detail: 'Sadaivvatsa' is read as Sadayavatsa; Matisāgara is taken as author on the catalogue's word alone, and the śāstrī as editor.

Name: Mahadandak Stotrapar Paryayalpabahutva Vichar Stavanam
Detail: Kept apart from Samayasundara's Alpabahutvagarbhita Mahāvīrastavana (j:600336) for want of an author, though the subject is the same and they may be one work.

Name: Avashyak Sutra Niryukterev Churni Part 01
Detail: 'Niryukterev Churni' is read as 'niryukter avacūrṇiḥ', the later Avacūrṇi, and so kept apart from Jinadāsa's Āvaśyakacūrṇi; Mānavijaya is taken as the 1965 editor.

Name: Nalayanam
Detail: Grouped with the other Nalāyana (j:600422) despite the different catalogue author.

Name: Mahopnishad
Detail: Read as the Upaniṣad in a modern Jain edition; Vijayakalyāṇabodhisūri is taken as editor, though the book may carry a Sanskrit commentary of his own or be a new work of his under this name.

Name: Kalpasutram
Detail: The catalogue's author is taken as the modern editor; any commentary in the edition is not named.

Name: Abhidhānacintāmaṇiṭīkā
Detail: j:t0004: Kept apart from the Abhidhānacintāmaṇi as its commentary; which ṭīkā the item carries is not stated, and the reader took it as Hemacandra's own.

Name: Anyoktiśataka
Detail: j:t0081: Authorship doubtful: Darśanavijaya may be the modern editor of the 1937 print.

Name: Ātmaśuddhopayoga
Detail: j:t0125: May be the same work as Buddhisāgarasūri's Śuddhopayoga (j:008664), which is not in this window.

Name: Āvaśyakaniryuktyavacūrṇi
Detail: j:t0137: Kept apart from Jinadāsa's Āvaśyakacūrṇi (d0136) on the reader's reading of the title as 'niryukter avacūrṇiḥ'; the metadata names no author, and the title could also be read as the Cūrṇi.

Name: Candraprabhacarita
Detail: j:t0206: One member, so not split here, but its items may be two works: j:022629 is Vīranandin's Digambara mahākāvya (Kāvyamālā); j:022638-9 (two parts, 592 pp., Śvetāmbara editor) are more likely the Śvetāmbara Devendrasūri's Candraprabhacaritra, and may belong with Candraprabhasvāmicarita.

Name: Candraprabhasvāmicarita
Detail: j:t0207: Kept apart from Candraprabhacarita (Vīranandin's): a Śvetāmbara edition, probably Devendrasūri's Candraprabhacaritra; the author is not named.

Name: Caraṇavyūhabhāṣya
Detail: j:t0216: Dossiers d0217 and d0218 grouped: both are the unnamed commentary printed with the Caraṇavyūha, and both readers took it to be Mahidāsa's, the usual printed one. Neither item names the commentator, so the identity is a judgement.

Name: Cāturmāsikavyākhyāna
Detail: j:t0223: The one member unites Vijayalakṣmīsūri's Āṣāḍhacāturmāsikavyākhyāna (j:034752) and a Gujarati translation of a Cāturmāsikavyākhyāna (j:034170), on the title alone.

Name: Dhanyacaritra
Detail: j:t0260: Dossier d0263 split: this item is titled padyam (verse) and names no author of the text, the other gadyabaddham (prose) by Jñānasāgara; different compositions on the story of Dhanya.

Name: Dharmaparīkṣā
Detail: j:t0271: Dossier d0272 split by author: the item names Jinamaṇḍana, not Padmasāgara or Yaśovijaya. The reading of the garbled author name is the reader's, so low.

Name: Dvādaśānuprekṣā
Detail: j:t0299: Dossier d0299 split by author: the item names Śubhacandra, not Kundakunda. Its identification as an extract of the Jñānārṇava is the reader's guess; it may be another text on the anuprekṣās.

Name: Hitopadeśa
Detail: j:t0358: Split from d0358: kept apart from Prabhānandasūri's Jain Hitopadeśa, whose item names a different author; identification with Nārāyaṇa's work rests on the title alone.

Name: Jambūsvāmicarita
Detail: j:t0414: Split from d0414: the item names neither Rājamalla nor Ratnaprabhasūri, and nothing says which of the two namesake works, if either, it carries; left apart for a human rather than assigned to one. | Dossier d0414 split in three. Name: Jambūsvāmicarita
Detail: j:t0415: Split from d0414: Ratnaprabhasūri is a different author from Rājamalla. Name: Nāgilacaritra
Detail: j:t0609: Dossier d0611 split on the catalogue's authors: j:020493 is given to Vardhamānasūri and j:600413 to Śubhaśīla Gaṇi. Both are 18-page pamphlets of 1935, so they may be one print catalogued twice with one author wrong; a human should check.

Name: Nāgilacaritra
Detail: j:t0610: Dossier d0611 split on the catalogue's authors: this item is given to Śubhaśīla Gaṇi, the other to Vardhamānasūri. Same title, year and page count, so possibly one print; a human should check.

Name: Nandīsūtramāhātmya
Detail: j:t0620: Kept apart from the Nandīsūtra: the title says Māhātmya, and the metadata does not show whether the book is the sūtra or a tract on it.

Name: Nandīvṛtti
Detail: j:t0622: Dossiers d0622 and d0624 grouped: the unnamed 'Nandi Sutra Tika' of j:020495 has 512 pages, against 514 for the 1924 edition of Malayagiri's vṛtti (j:600244), and its reader already took it as probably Malayagiri's. The identification rests on the page count alone.

Name: Nandīvṛttidurgapadavyākhyā
Detail: j:t0623: comments_on renamed from the reader's 'Nandīvṛtti' to Nandīsūtravivaraṇa, Haribhadra's commentary, so that it is not taken for Malayagiri's Nandīvṛtti in this window. That the item carries this gloss is the reader's uncertain reading of the catalogue's 'Chandrasuri'.

Name: Parāga
Detail: j:t0717: The reader gives the author as j:p0500 Lāvaṇyasūri; the Pramodā in this window, by the same modern monk, carries j:p0994 Vijayalāvaṇyasūri. The two person keys probably name one man. Whether the 84-page item carries the Parāga at all is uncertain.

Name: Paramātmadarśana
Detail: j:t0719: Same title and author, so kept together; the 1910 book of 432 pages and the short work in the 206-page Pañcagranthasaṅgraha may not be the same composition. | Same title and author in both items, though the 1910 book of 432 pages is far longer than the share of a five-work volume of 206 pages; the two may differ in extent or carry a commentary.

Name: Paryuṣaṇāṣṭāhnikavyākhyāna
Detail: j:t0733: Grouped d0735 and d0736 on the title alone, with no author or date to tell them apart; Maṇivijaya's j:600358 and Guṇasāgarasūri's translation j:600203 may be other Aṣṭāhnikavyākhyānas than Kṣamākalyāṇa's. | Grouped d0735 and d0736: the same generic title with no evidence of a different composition; only one item names an author (Kṣamākalyāṇa), and Maṇivijaya on j:600358 may be editor or author of another sermon. A later step may split.

Name: Prakaraṇapuṣpamālā
Detail: j:t0753: Kept apart from the Prakaraṇasamuccaya (d0760), also under Ratnasiṃhasūri's name: the titles differ and neither item names its contents.

Name: Prakaraṇaratna
Detail: j:t0754: Kept apart from the Prakaraṇaratnākara (d0759) of the same publisher: the names differ and nothing shows the contents are the same.

Name: Prakaraṇaratnākara
Detail: j:t0755: Kept apart from the Prakaraṇaratna (d0758) of the same publisher: the names differ and nothing shows the contents are the same.

Name: Prakaraṇasamuccaya
Detail: j:t0756: Kept apart from the Prakaraṇapuṣpamālā (d0757), also under Ratnasiṃhasūri's name: the titles differ and neither item names its contents.

Name: Pratyākhyānasvarūpa
Detail: j:t0793: One member rests on a title cut off at 'Pratyā', read as the Pratyākhyānasvarūpa from the same publisher and year as the other item.

Name: Raṇasiṃhacaritra
Detail: j:t0824: Split d0831: this printing names a Somagaṇi as author, the other Śubhaśīla Gaṇi; different authors and lengths (72 against 30 pages). The name is garbled, so the split is a judgement call.

Name: Raṇasiṃhacaritra
Detail: j:t0825: Split d0831: Śubhaśīla Gaṇi is named as author here, a Somagaṇi on the other printing.

Name: Ratnapālacaritra
Detail: j:t0833: Grouped d0839 and d0840: the same tale under Ratnapālacaritra and Ratnapālanṛpacaritra, neither with a named author; nothing in the metadata shows two compositions, but the page counts differ widely, hence low.

Name: Śāntināthacaritra
Detail: j:t0928: Grouped d0936 and d0937: Śāntināthacarita and Śāntināthacaritra under Ajitaprabha are one work. p1-catalogue-002:t68 (item j:004339, 'Amrutsuri', 1965, 388 pp.) names no old author and may be another Śāntināthacaritra (Munibhadra, Bhāvacandra, Māṇikyacandra); it is grouped here on the name alone, hence low.

Name: Śreṇikacaritra
Detail: j:t1030: Kept as one by the title; nothing in the 1905 item's metadata shows a different composition, but nothing confirms it is Devendrasūri's either. | Kept as one by the rule for identical names, since the second item names no author; but the extents (44 pp. complete against 262 pp. for a first part) suggest two compositions. For review.

Name: Śrīpālacaritra
Detail: j:t1033: Split from d1046 and left on its own: the item names only a modern editor, and with three differently authored Śrīpālacaritras in the window there is no ground for choosing one. | Dossier d1046 split by author. This member has no author, and its 334-page item fits none of the three attributed versions for certain (the others run 36-100 pp.), so it is left on its own rather than joined to one of them by guess.

Name: Sūktamuktāvalī
Detail: j:t1083: Dossier d1094 split: ascribed to an old teacher, earlier and of different extent than Bhūpendrasūri's compilation. A judgement call; it may deserve regrouping if the two prove to be one book.

Name: Vardhamānadeśanā
Detail: j:t1226: Kept as one entity because the items do not let the Prakrit and the Sanskrit version be told apart; a later step may split by version.

Name: Vargacūlikā
Detail: j:t1229: Grouped d1247 (Vargacūlikā, 2010 edition) and d1243 (Vaṅkacūliyā summary, 1923): taken as the same Vaggacūliyā/Vaṅgacūliyā under two spellings; no author on either side, so a judgement call.

Name: Vastusāra
Detail: j:t1233: Grouped d1251 and d1252: items j:022760 and j:035332 are plainly two scans of one 1956 book (same title, 26 and 25 pp.), catalogued once as वस्तुसार and once as वास्तुसार. Which spelling is right, and whether it is a vāstu text, is open.

Name: Bālabrahmacārī Yogirāja
Detail: j:p0062: 'Bālabrahmacārī Yogirāja' is an epithet, not a name; kept as an entry of its own because the person behind it cannot be identified.

Name: Bālacandrasūri
Detail: j:p0064: Split from d0064: a modern Kharatara monk, seven centuries later than the Vivekamañjarī commentator. His role on j:020453 is the reader's guess.

Name: Buddhimuni
Detail: j:p0119: Kept apart from Buddhisāgara Gaṇi (d0124–d0126) because the name differs, but the Kharatara Gaṇi Buddhimuni, pupil of Keśaramuni, may well be the same monk.

Name: Candrasāgarasūri
Detail: j:p0133: Grouped d0140 and d0141 on the name, the years and the line: Candrasāgara Gaṇi, pupil of Sāgarānandasūri, edited the Siddhahema and was later sūri. The metadata does not confirm that the Gaṇi of 1948 is the Sūri of 1951.

Name: Dānavijaya Gaṇi
Detail: j:p0164: Either the c. 1700 author of the Dānadīpikā on the Kalpasūtra or a modern Dānavijaya as editor; the metadata does not say.

Name: Darśanavijaya
Detail: j:p0166: Kept as one: all three items are prints of 1937–1943 or undated under the bare name, and nothing in the metadata separates them. If the Anyoktiśataka is the 17th-c. Darśanavijaya Gaṇi's, p1-catalogue-004:darshanavijaya is a second person. | Kept as one: all three items are 20th-c. prints under the bare name Darshanvijay. The Anyoktiśataka may instead be by a 17th-c. Darśanavijayagaṇi, with the name on the 1937 print being his, not an editor's; nothing in the metadata settles it.

Name: Devacandra
Detail: j:p0174: Split from d0185: a 20th-c. translator, not the 18th-c. Kharatara Devacandra. He may be the same as Devacandra Kacchī (d0186), a Kacchī Sthānakavāsī monk of that time, but only the name suggests it, so they are left apart.

Name: Devavijaya Gaṇi
Detail: j:p0189: Split from d0198 on the role alone: as editor of a printed collection he would be modern. If he is a commentator he could be the 16th-c. Devavijaya Gaṇi after all.

Name: Harṣavijaya
Detail: j:p0299: Kept as one dossier on the name: nothing in the metadata separates an author Harṣavijaya from the modern editor, though they may well be two.

Name: Hemacandrasūri
Detail: j:p0306: Left apart from Hemacandra (d0321): a 2004 poem on a modern monk cannot be the 12th-c. polymath's. Which modern Hemacandrasūri is a judgement.

Name: Hemahaṃsa Gaṇi
Detail: j:p0307: Dossiers d0324 and d0325 grouped: the grammarian and the Ārambhasiddhi commentator are the same 15th-c. Tapāgaccha Hemahaṃsa Gaṇi. The member read from the Kathāratnākara is kept here because the catalogue writes this name, though that work is Hemavijaya Gaṇi's (entity for him is separate); a human may prefer to move it. | Grouped d0324 and d0325: the same name, spelled as one word or two, with the same gaccha and century. The Kathāratnākara reading (p1-catalogue-001:p35) stays here because the catalogue names Hemahaṃsa, though the work may be Hemavijaya's. Pandit has him twice (85758, 86723).

Name: Hīrālāla Śāstrī
Detail: j:p0321: The 1918–19 Benares Supāsanāhacariya is known as Haragovindadāsa T. Śeṭha's edition; "Hiralal Shastri" may be a catalogue slip, but the name is kept as written.

Name: Jayasāgara
Detail: j:p0363: Kept apart from Jayasāgara Upādhyāya (d0387) and the 20th-c. Jayasāgarasūri (d0386): the name alone does not say which, if either, he is.

Name: Jinasūra Muni
Detail: j:p0393: Grouped d0418 and d0419 on the reading of the catalogue's Jinsuri as Jinasūra, to whom a Rūpasenacaritra is ascribed; the metadata does not confirm it, and Jinasūri may be another man. | Grouped d0418 and d0419: the Rūpasenacaritra's 'Jinsuri' is taken as Jinasūra, to whom a Rūpasenacaritra is ascribed beside the Priyaṅkaranṛpakathā; from memory, not confirmed by Pandit, and no context disagrees.

Name: Kanakavijaya
Detail: j:p0430: Grouped d0459 and d0460: same name and the same year, 1940, and nothing in the context tells them apart; but the name is common among modern monks.

Name: Kīrtiratnavijaya
Detail: j:p0457: Probably the same man as a Ratnakīrtivijaya elsewhere in the registry; none is in this window.

Name: Labdhisūri
Detail: j:p0484: Grouped d0522 and d0523. The reader of the Mūrtimaṇḍana already identifies its Labdhivijaya as the later Vijayalabdhisūri. The Labdhivijaya of the Merutrayodaśīkathā (1916) is kept with him on the name and the compatible date alone; he could be an earlier namesake.

Name: Labdhivijaya Gaṇi
Detail: j:p0485: Kept apart from Labdhisūri (Labdhivijaya of the Tapāgaccha): the book is a Kharatara one and his part in it is unknown. The date would also suit the Tapāgaccha Labdhivijaya, so this may be the same man.

Name: Mānatuṅgasūri
Detail: j:p0534: Dossier kept whole and apart from d0576. Only the author of the Jayantīprakaraṇa is identified; the authors of the Aparājitakathānaka (j:034168) and the Mānatuṅgaśāstra (j:008422) are not, and either could be another Mānatuṅga, the Bhaktāmara poet included. Nothing in the metadata separates them. | Split d0577: these two members are left together on the identical name, with nothing in the items to identify the man or to tell the two apart. Either may belong to the Bhaktāmara Mānatuṅga or to the Mānatuṅgasūri of the Jayantīprakaraṇa. | Split d0577: the author of the Jayantīprakaraṇa is dated c. 1200 by his pupil Malayaprabha's commentary, and is set apart from the two Mānatuṅgasūris whose works are unidentified. | Overlapping windows decided these members differently; taken as the union of the two: p2a-008 Mānatuṅgasūri (3); p2a-007 Mānatuṅgasūri (2); p2a-007 Mānatuṅgasūri (1)

Name: Mānavijaya
Detail: j:p0536: Split d0578 from the 17th-c. Mānavijaya. The four modern readings are kept together on the name; the two of 1924 are surely one man, but editions spread over 1924–1965 may be the work of two monks of the name, and on the Jainatattvasāra (1941) 'Manvijay Gani' could be an older commentator. | Split d0578: modern editors, apart from the 17th-c. author. The two editions of 1924 are surely one man's; those of 1941, 1952 and 1965 may be another modern monk's, and on j:600374 'Manvijay Gani' could be the commentator rather than the editor.

Name: Nemicandragaṇi
Detail: j:p0621: Kept apart from the other Nemicandras of the window: different gaccha and work; identity and date uncertain.

Name: Nemicandrasūri
Detail: j:p0623: Dossier d0667 split: the author of the Sukhabodhā (Nemicandra alias Devendragaṇi, fl. 1073-1085) is set apart as an earlier namesake of the same gaccha. Pandit 85410 holds both works under one person, so the split is a judgement call.

Name: Nemicandrasūri (Devendragaṇi)
Detail: j:p0624: Split from dossier d0667: the reader joined him with the author of the Pravacanasāroddhāra, who is usually held to be a later Nemicandra (pupil of Āmradeva, fl. c. 1160). Pandit 85410 conflates the two; if they are one, merge with that entity.

Name: Prabhācandra
Detail: j:p0661: Split from dossier d0705 (the Śvetāmbara author of the Prabhāvakacarita set apart). The author of the Kathākośa is kept with the logician: same sect, place and century, an identification often but not universally made.

Name: Pūrṇacandrasāgarasūri
Detail: j:p0688: Dossiers d0733 and d0734 grouped: same name and lineage, the later form with the title sūri gained after 2005; not confirmed by the metadata. | Grouped d0733 and d0734: same name, same Sāgara line, eight years apart; the -sūri of 2013 is taken as the rank the editor of 2005 later received. Nothing in the metadata confirms it.

Name: Rājaśekharasūri
Detail: j:p0700: Split from d0745 (a modern editor of 1992 and 2002 books, not the 14th-c. author) and grouped with d0746, whose reader identifies Rājaśekharavijaya as the later Rājaśekharasūri. The identity of the monk and the ācārya rests on that reader and on what is known of him, not on the metadata.

Name: Rāmaśarman
Detail: j:p0719: Kept apart from Rāmāśrama (d0767), the author of the Siddhāntacandrikā: the name as written is Rāmaśarman, read as an editor, though it may be a slip for the author.

Name: Ratnacandra Gaṇi
Detail: j:p0734: Kept apart from the Śatāvadhānī Ratnacandra although both are written "Ratnachandra Maharaj": the item is the Adhyātmakalpadruma, on which the 17th-c. Gaṇi wrote the commentary printed in 1940. The name could instead be a modern editor or translator.

Name: Śāntisūri
Detail: j:p0789: Split the dossier 'Śāntisūri': the Tilakamañjarīṭippaṇaka is by Śāntisūri of the Pūrṇatallagaccha, a different man, set apart. The rest are kept together on the name and on Pandit 85390, which gives the Śiṣyahitā, Jīvavicāra and Dharmaratnaprakaraṇa to one Śāntisūri; the authors of the Jīvavicāra (one reader says Bṛhadgaccha) and of the Ceiyavandaṇamahābhāsa may be other Śāntisūris of the 11th-12th c.

Name: Siddhasenasūri
Detail: j:p0813: Kept apart from Siddhasena Divākara: the Namaskāramāhātmya is a medieval work by a later Siddhasenasūri; the metadata gives only the name.

Name: Śrīcandrasūri
Detail: j:p0844: Split the dossier 'Śrīcandrasūri'. These two members are kept together: the pupil of Dhaneśvarasūri is credited with both the Nandī gloss and the Nirayāvalikā commentary and Sāmācārī. The pupil of Maladhārī Hemacandra is set apart. Pandit 85487 runs the two together. The identifications rest on bare 'Chandrasuri' and a garbled 'Macchindracharya' in the metadata. | Split from dossier d0898: the glossator of the Nandīvṛtti and the author of the Nirayāvalikāvṛtti and Subodhā Sāmācārī are one man, the pupil of Dhaneśvarasūri, distinct from the Maladhāri author of the Muṇisuvvayasāmicariya. 'Macchindracharya' on the Subodhasāmācārī is a reader's reading of a garbled Śrīcandrācārya. Pandit 85487 conflates the two namesakes.

Name: Śrīcandrasūri
Detail: j:p0845: Split from the dossier 'Śrīcandrasūri': the pupil of Maladhārī Hemacandra, a contemporary namesake of the pupil of Dhaneśvarasūri. | Split from dossier d0898 on lineage: the pupil of Maladhārī Hemacandra is kept apart from his contemporary, the pupil of Dhaneśvarasūri. Pandit 85487 (Candrasūri, 1180) lists works of both men under one record, so no hint is given.

Name: Sūracandra Gaṇi
Detail: j:p0878: Groups dossiers d0937 and d0938. Two members are surely the author of the Jainatattvasāra; the third, the Sūracandra named with Rājakīrti Gaṇi on the Vardhamānadeśanā (j:009650), is kept with them on the name and on Rājakīrti's being a Kharatara of the same century, with nothing to confirm it.

Name: Sūryamalla Yati
Detail: j:p0884: Groups dossiers d0944 and d0945 on the name and the period alone: the Sāgarotpatti of 'Suryamal Maharaj' (1926) and the Jainaratnasāra of 'Suryamalla Yati' (1941). Nothing in the metadata confirms or contradicts that they are one man. Sūryamuni (d0946) is kept apart.

Name: Vāgbhaṭa
Detail: j:p0940: Split from dossier d1003: the poet of the Neminirvāṇa is usually distinguished from the author of the Vāgbhaṭālaṃkāra, though the identity has been proposed; a judgement call.

Name: Vardhamānasūri
Detail: j:p0953: Split from dossier d1015. The separately printed caritras of 1928-1935 are taken as extracts from the 13th-c. Vāsupūjyacaritra; for the Sūracandra-, Nāgila- and Candrayaśaścaritra this is a presumption from the like title, date and format. Member p1-catalogue-004:vardhamanasuri also covers a Ghaṇṭākarṇapratiṣṭhāvidhi (j:020345), which may rather belong to the Vardhamānasūri of the Ācāradinakara; the member cannot be divided and is placed here by its caritra.

Name: Vijayānandasūri
Detail: j:p0998: Two readers' uncertain entries under one name, kept together for want of evidence to split: a Granthatrayī (1999) and a verse Dhanyacaritra. Whether either is Ātmārāma (Vijayānandasūri, 1837-1896) or a later ācārya of the name is not settled. | Two low-confidence readings of the same catalogue name on unidentified books; kept as one for want of evidence that they differ, but they may be two persons.

Name: Vijayomaṅgasūri
Detail: j:p1008: Dossiers d0992 (Umaṅgasūri, 1937) and d0993 (Umaṅgavijaya Gaṇi, 1932) grouped as one monk before and after becoming ācārya: both are editors of Prakrit texts in the 1930s, five years apart. Not confirmed by the metadata; a judgement call.

Name: Vinayasāgara
Detail: j:p1022: Split from dossier d1081: the Hiṅgulaprakaraṇa is an older didactic work by an Upādhyāya Vinayasāgara, not a writing of the modern Kharatara scholar (1929–2014) whom the other three members name as editor and essayist.

Name: Vīravijaya
Detail: j:p1032: Kept as one on the name alone. The Praśnacintāmaṇi's author is Pandit's Vīravijaya Gaṇi (86174); the Vīravijaya on the 1938 Adhyātmasāra may be the same (a ṭabo on that text goes under the name) or a 20th-c. editor.

Name: Yaśodeva Upādhyāya
Detail: j:p1063: Kept apart from Yaśovijaya, as its reader did, and from Yaśodevasūri of the Pākṣikasūtravṛtti (d1122), who is of another gaccha; Pandit's Yaśodeva Sūri (85417) unites the works of both, so the two Yaśodevas may be one.

Name: Yaśovijaya
Detail: j:p1066: Split from dossier d1125: these two readers took 'Yashovijay-2' on two volumes of 1976 as the modern editor. He did edit such volumes, but everywhere else in the window the catalogue's Yashovijay-2 is the Upādhyāya himself (editions of 1915–1946 among them), so the name on these two items probably means the author too, and this entry may need merging into the Upādhyāya.

Name: बिस्मिलस्य बलिदान-कथा
Detail: A short modern Sanskrit prose piece on the martyrdom of Ram Prasad Bismil; taken as a modern essay, not a work of the tradition.

Name: योगपादः
Detail: The title names only a division, the yogapāda of an āgama. Its five subpages match the five adhyāyas of the Pādmasaṃhitā's yogapāda, and the Pādmasaṃhitā page is a stub with four subpages; mapped there on that ground alone.

Name: किञ्चित्तन्त्रम्
Detail: The title means only 'a certain tantra': the page does not name its text.

Name: कुलानन्दादि
Detail: The title is 'the Kulānanda and others': a group of short texts beginning with the Kulānandatantra, the rest unnamed. Only the Kulānandatantra can be mapped.

Name: परात्रिंशिका (तत्त्वविवेकाख्यव्याख्योपेता)
Detail: The commentary 'called Tattvaviveka' is taken as Abhinavagupta's Vivaraṇa (Tattvavivaraṇa); the page names no author.

Name: परात्रिंशिकाविवृतिः (तत्त्वविवेकाख्यव्याख्योपेता)
Detail: Nearly the same size as परात्रिंशिका (तत्त्वविवेकाख्यव्याख्योपेता) and with the same description; taken as the same commentary, Abhinavagupta's. If Tattvaviveka is a gloss on the Vivṛti, a further title is needed.

Name: प्रत्यभिज्ञादर्शनम्
Detail: A page of 107 bytes named for a school, the Pratyabhijñā philosophy; a stub or landing page, not a text.

Name: भावचूडामणिः (श्रीमहामहेश्वरेण कृतः)
Detail: 'Made by Śrī Mahāmaheśvara' is read as Śiva, the tantra's speaker, not a human author. Grouped with भावचूडामणिः on the title, though this page is nine times as long.

Name: सिद्धान्तशिरोमणिः तत्त्वप्रदीपिकासहितः
Detail: The page says Siddhāntaśiromaṇi, which is Bhāskara's astronomy; but it is filed among tantra texts and carries a Tattvapradīpikā, which is Maritoṇṭadārya's commentary on the Vīraśaiva Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi. Taken as that work, with the title a slip.

Name: सुबोधमञ्जरी
Detail: Title alone; work and author not identified.

Name: स्वातन्त्र्यदीपिका (महामहेश्वराचार्यकृता)
Detail: The author is given only as Mahāmaheśvarācārya, an epithet and not a name; left unplaced.

Name: भृगुसंहिता
Detail: Filed under Vaikhānasāgama; kept apart from Kriyādhikāra, Prakīrṇādhikāra and Yajñādhikāra, though it may be one of Bhṛgu's adhikāras under the general name (it has 37 subpages, as the Prakīrṇādhikāra does).

Name: अनुत्तरप्रकाशिका
Detail: Anuttaraprakāśikā taken as Ādyanātha's Anuttaraprakāśapañcāśikā, from the title and the size.

Name: कल्पवृक्षः
Detail: Title alone; work not identified.

Name: कालोत्तरम्-शिवागमः
Detail: Which recension of the Kālottara is not said; grouped with the Sārdhatriśatikālottara as one work.

Name: गोरक्षशतकम् (हठयोगगोरक्षशतकम्)
Detail: Grouped with the other Gorakṣaśataka page; the parenthesis (Haṭhayogagorakṣaśataka) may mark the other of the two texts of this name.

Name: शिवसूत्रवार्तिका
Detail: Two Vārttikas on the Śivasūtra exist (Bhāskara's and Varadarāja's); the page does not say which.

Name: सार्थत्रिशतिकालोत्तरागमः
Detail: The Sārdhatriśati recension of the Kālottara; grouped with the Kālottara as a recension.

Name: जाबालोपनिषत् (सामवेदः)
Detail: Split from the Yajurveda Jābālopaniṣad because the page assigns it to the Sāmaveda (the Jābālyupaniṣad); the two pages are almost the same size, so it may be a duplicate.

Name: नृसिंहतापनी उपनिषद्-1
Detail: Grouped with the Nṛsiṃhottaratāpanīya as one Nṛsiṃhatāpanīyopaniṣad, as the Muktikā counts it; they are often counted as two upaniṣads.

Name: नृसिंहोत्तरतापनीयोपनिषद
Detail: Grouped with the Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīya as one Nṛsiṃhatāpanīyopaniṣad, as the Muktikā counts it; they are often counted as two upaniṣads.

Name: भावोपनिषत्
Detail: Bhāvopaniṣad taken as the Bhāvanopaniṣad, from the size and the tantric uploads around it.

Name: A Dictionary of Sanskrit Grammar
Detail: A modern reference dictionary in English, so not a Sanskrit work; its author is named only in the scan's file name. It could instead be counted as a work.
